This appears to be a CBP ruling on a Halloween costume. Adult costumes of textile materials are classified in 6211.43 (women's garments of man-made fibers) if they are not festive articles of chapter 95, but the ruling's treatment depends on the construction of the garments.

Under note 1(e) to Chapter 95 and Chapter 61/62 rules, costumes made of textile fabrics that are not "carnival" articles of 9505 can be classified as ordinary apparel. Since 2000, CBP has held that costumes of ordinary construction are classified under 62 when they are wearing apparel. A pullover top and skirt would be classified as a set, but the set rules for 6104 or 6204 require a suit or ensemble. The costume also includes a headband, a sash and Tarot cards, which are not garments. The set would not be classified as a set of apparel, so the classification would go by the essential character of the garments.

CBP has ruled that Halloween costumes of this kind are classified in 9505.90.6000 (festive articles, other). Adult-size costumes in particular have been treated as 9505 when they are not ordinary apparel. Here the description lists a top, skirt, hip sash, headband and Tarot cards, a themed costume sold as a retail set. The Tarot cards support the festive classification, and CBP generally classifies such a costume as a festive article in 9505.90.6000.
